caseno: Criminal Misc. Case Nos. 5866 of 1998, 5867 of 1998 and 5865 of 1998.
lawyer:
Khandaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Khondaker Mahboob Hossain and Humayun Kabir Bulbul, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners.
Mahmudul Islam, Attorney-General, Md Faruq, Deputy Attorney-General ----- For the State.
parties:
KM Obaidur Rahman and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
State, through the Deputy Commissioner Dhaka ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Karim J: These three Rules were issued in Criminal Misc. Case No. 5866/1998, 5865/1998, 5867/1998 directing Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to show cause as to why petitioner KM Obaidur Rahman, Md Nurul Islam Manjoor and Shah Moazzam Hossain respectively should not be enlarged on bail in Lalbagh PS Case No.II dated 4-11-95 corresponding to GR Case No. 10698 of 1975 now pending before the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka. We propose to dispose of all the three Rules by this judgment. The Rules were issued after rejection of the prayer for bail by the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka. 

 3. The prosecution case, in short, is that, after the killing of Bangabandhu Sk Mujibor Rahman and his family on 15th August, 1975, pressure was brought to bear upon Syed Nazrul Islam, Captain Munsur Ali, Tajuddin Ahmed and AHM Kamruzzaman to join the cabinet of Khondakar Moshtaque Ahmed, who was then the President, but decline of the offer resulted in their arrest and confinement in Dhaka Central Jail on 23-8-1995. The charge sheet further mentions that considering these four political leaders as a threat to the survival of the Moshtaque Government, the accused persons entered into a criminal conspiracy to kill them and in pursuance of this conspiracy Captain Moslemuddin and a group of armed persons entered into the jail and killed the four leaders between 4.00 AM and 4-35 AM on the night following 2-11-1975. It is alleged that the three petitioners, who were Ministers of State in the cabinet of Khondaker Moshtaque Ahmed, were a party to this criminal conspiracy. 

 4. Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for KM Obaidur Rahman, submits that the, investigation of the case has failed to collect any material or evidence to establish involvement of the petitioner with the Jail killing. He submits that the President could call any Minister or Minsters of State at any time for state business and more closeness to the President. Without any tangible evidence, does not prove that the petitioner was a party to any criminal conspiracy for killing four political leaders. He submits that KM Obaidur Rahman was arrested on 29-9-98 and falsely implicated in the case to harass and humiliate him. He is a Member of Parliament and he lives with his family in Bangladesh and there is no question of his abscondence if the prayer for bail is allowed. The learned Counsel further mentions that being in advanced age, KM Obaidur Rahman suffered a massive cardiac attack on 15-8-1997 and is a diabetic taking insulin twice a day and an acute ulcer was detected in his lower abdomen in March, 1994, for which he has to take medicine regularly. 

 5. Mr. Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, appearing for petitioner Md Nurul Islam Manjoor, submits that like KM Obaidur Rahman, this petitioner resigned from the Cabinet of Khondaker Moshtaque Ahmed on 3-11-1975 without any involvement in any criminal conspiracy for killing any person or the four political leaders and the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case for political victimisation as like KM Obaidur Rahman he also left Awami League and joined BNP. The learned Advocate submits that petitioner Md Nurul Islam Manjoor withdrew from political activities and engaged himself in industry and commerce with no chance of abscondence if the prayer for bail is allowed. He suffers from ischemic heart disease and suffered anginal attack and received treatment in Bangkok and Singapore. 

 6. Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, appearing for petitioner Shah Moazzem Hossain, adopted the arguments of Mr. Khondaker Mahbubuddin Ahmed on behalf of the other two petitioners. He submits that all the three petitioners, who were ministers of State, resigned from the Cabinet of Khondaker Moshtaque Ahmed on 4-11-1975 thereby distancing themselves from the incident of Jail Killing, and has produced photo copies of The Daily Ittefaq and Dainik Bangla dated 5-11-1975 in support of these resignations. Mr. Bhuiyan contends that the petitioner was arrested and falsely implicated in this case though the investigation disclosed no material or evidence against him, only because he is taking an active role against the present Government. Aged over 60 years petitioners Shah Moazzem Hossain is a heart patient and suffering from diabetes, piles and high blood pressure. Mr. Khondaker Mahbub Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for petitioner Shah Moazzem Hossain, submits that the nature of accusation and heinousness of the crime are not the only circumstances to be taken into consideration under sections 496 and 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the other relevant circumstances like the chance of absconding, tampering with evidence or hindering the course of trial should also be considered in disposing of an application for bail. Mr. Khondakar contends there is no chance of abscondence by Shah Moazzem Hossain who is a prominent political figure, and the investigation has already been concluded with no chance of tampering with evidence. 

 8. We have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State and read the confessional statement of co-accused Taheruddin Thakur under section 164 CrPC and the statement of the witnesses recorded under section 161 CrPC. It appears from these statements, the first information report and the charge-sheet that the persons accused in this case fall in three groups, namely, those who talked with the Deputy Inspector-General and Inspector General of Prisons over the phone from Bangabhaban on the night of 3-11-76, those of the army personal who left Bangabhaban, entered into the jail and killed the four political leaders, and lastly, those who are alleged to have entered into a criminal conspiracy to kill the four political leaders inside the jail. We gather from the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Deputy Attorney-General that the three petitioners belong to the third group of accused persons. 

 10. The learned Counsel for the petitioner have referred to the decision in the case of Khalid Saigol vs State 14 DLR (SC) 321 for the argument that heinousness of the crime alleged, though a material circumstance, is not the only criterion to decide an application for bail and that the other circumstances like the chance of the accused absconding, tampering with evidence or hindering the prosecution of the case should also be taken into consideration. 

 11. Under sub-section (1) of section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an accused may not be released on bail if there appear reasonable grounds for believing that he has been guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life. The proviso to the sub-section contains exceptions to cases of a person being under the age of sixteen years, of a woman or any sick person. 

 13. Appearing at the fag-end of the arguments. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, learned Attorney-General, has submitted that very influential persons as they are once out of jail on bail, the petitioners will use of all the influence and power for tampering with the evidence and threatening witnesses. He submits that the government has provided the petitioners with all medical facilities and care and are ready to shift any of them to Bangabandhu Medical University Hospital or Suhrawardy Hospital in case of critical illness. 

 15. We have perused the statement of co-accused Taheruddin Thakur recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure mentioning consultation by President Moshtaque Ahmed with the army officers (accused in the Jail killing case) and the petitioners towards the end of October, 1975. The President also had discussion with the maker of the statement (under section 164). The statement states that at that time decision was made for killing the four political leaders inside the jail. "But the President never sat together with all for such consultation."It is for the trial Court to piece together all the fragments of the evidence. Reading this statement and the statements of some of the witnesses recorded under section 161 CrPC we do not allow the prayer for bail made on behalf of the three petitioners inasmuch as there appear reasonable grounds for believing that they may be a party to a criminal conspiracy as alleged by the prosecution, but at the same time we direct the opposite party (State) to make all necessary arrangements for medical care and attention of the petitioners who are aged and said to be suffering from various ailments. 

 Any observations made by us for disposal of this bail matter will have no bearing on the disposal of the case on merit by the trial Court.
